sources.title: A. M. Chowdhury, Sena Dynasty, Banglapedia
sources.note: Asiatic Society of Bangladesh encyclopedia. Indexed original article read, including origins, Vijayasena, Vallalasena, Lakshmanasena and descendants. Direct page currently returns an uninformative response. The opening range circa 1097 to 1225 is less nuanced than the concluding evidence for later eastern survival; public copy therefore avoids an exact final extinction date. No assertion of conquest of every modern Bengali-speaking territory.

sources.title: Deopara stone inscription of Vijayasena, edited and translated by Ryosuke Furui
sources.note: DHARMA scholarly edition read directly: Sanskrit, Gaudi script, opening invocation; verses 20 to 22 campaigns/fleet, 25 to 29 temple and lake, 35 to 36 poet and engraver. Edition checked by editor against photographs at Indian Museum in 2011. This researcher verified published transcription and translation, not original glyphs. Individual inscription treated as its own primary work.

sources.title: Tarpandighi plate of Lakshmanasena, year 2, edited and translated by Ryosuke Furui
sources.note: DHARMA direct reading, especially lines 32 to 49. Boundaries include Nicadahara pond, Nandiharipa reservoir, Mollana canal and land for a Buddhist establishment. Grant includes trees and specified rights; recipient is Isvaradevasarman, trained in Kauthuma Samaveda observance. Year 2 reading differs from an older year 3 reading; no exact CE date is forced.

sources.title: Naihati plate of Vallalasena, year 11, edited and translated by Ryosuke Furui
sources.note: DHARMA direct reading, stanza 14 and lines 29 to 56: royal mother Vilasadevi, solar-eclipse donation; named village boundaries, homesteads/cultivation/fallow, 500 puranas in cowries annual production, and royal fiscal rights. Distinct primary inscription, not an additional budget for a duplicate of the Tarpandighi charter.

sources.title: British Museum: Copper plate with inscription
sources.note: Museum-authored collection description read directly on Google Arts & Culture. Single copper sheet, Sanskrit, ten-armed Shiva seal; grant to Udayakaradeva Sharman as fee for ritual for queen Vilasa Devi. Header says 1129 but prose calculates 1159 for regnal year 32; only twelfth-century context used. Same object as British Museum 1957,1121.1; canonical-work reuse checked against both URLs.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum: Durga Slaying the Demon Buffalo Mahisha, 1993.7
sources.note: Direct object metadata plus indexed original curatorial paragraph. Twelfth-century Bengal, Pala-Sena period, argillite, height 13.5 cm, sixteen arms. Not assigned to a named ruler or an excavated private household.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum: Brhaspati, Personification of Jupiter, 47.29
sources.note: Direct museum metadata: Sena dynasty, twelfth century, Bihar/Bengal or Bangladesh, stone, 55.9 cm tall. Shows planetary personification, not evidence of telescopes, a new astronomical discovery or a specific royal commission.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Kolkata Circle: Ruins of Fort, Bamanpukur
sources.note: Indexed official original read; direct fetch failed. ASI describes 1982 to 1988 excavations, tenth to twelfth century remains, a Panchayatana temple complex, possible Buddhist stucco affiliation and ritual copper objects. Name Ballaldhipi does not establish a royal residence or attribute every layer to Ballala Sena.

sources.title: Tamal Dutta, Ballal Dhipi in Nadia District of West Bengal: An Archaeological Overview, 2021
sources.note: Research article read directly. Only the observed drainage description on printed page 15 is used: lime plaster, channels for rainwater, basalt crocodile-faced outlet. Its historical section and its interpretation of the Tarpandighi grant contain problems, so they are not used. No precise Sena-period assignment of the outlet or modern working-condition guarantee.

sources.title: Jaydev and Gitagovindam, Banglapedia
sources.note: Indexed institutional original by Kanailal Ray and Paresh Chandra Mandal. Court association, disputed biography, poem of Radha and Krishna, twelve cantos and twenty-four songs with indicated ragas, later influence. Public paragraph avoids selecting a disputed birthplace.

sources.title: Shahanara Husain, Saduktikarnamrita, Banglapedia
sources.note: Indexed institutional original read: Shridharadasa compilation in 1205, after imported map endpoint, drawing on older and contemporary poetry. Public passage explicitly marks its later date and avoids treating every poem as a contemporary Sena eyewitness report.

sources.title: Human History Map: imported Senas geometry
sources.note: Locally decoded source geometry. Both 1000 to 1100 and 1100 to 1200 outlines have bounds approximately 91.302 to 94.679 E and 20.573 to 27.668 N. The polygon is east of the Bengal heartland documented by inscriptions and political histories; no geometry changes made.

proposedOverrides.name: Senas
proposedOverrides.summary: A powerful Bengal dynasty known through land grants, art and poetry.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed record, no related runtime or staged alias found. Distinct from Pala and later Bengal Sultanate narratives.
batchIdentityNotes.mapWarning: Source outline east of Sena Bengal; starts before well-documented late-eleventh-century emergence and ends before early-thirteenth-century contraction. No geometry, index or date mutation proposed.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Verified namaḥ śivāya in DHARMA transcription and translation of Deopara line 1; Gaudi original script, modern Roman transliteration. No visual reading claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceScope: Individual inscriptions are distinct primary works. Temple water outlet has uncertain phase and is labeled as contextual evidence at a multiphase site. No healthcare system, household toilet or universal school is invented.
